C0.quote: we define a general notion of the veto core
C0.note: Single-winner ranked voting rules electing from a generalized veto core with metric distortion 3.

C1.quote: also satisfies resolvability, monotonicity, majority, majority loser, mutual majority and reversal symmetry
C1.note: Main results: characterization of the (p,q)-veto core via matchings and SerialVeto (Thms 1-3), tied-winner property of SimultaneousVeto (Thm 4), and axioms plus distortion-3 guarantee (Thm 5). Algorithms are presented but no complexity results, so AL not coded.

C2.3.quote: captures how much the voter dislikes the candidate
C2.3.note: Voters have positions in a metric space (distances to candidates), defined separately from rankings.

C2.4.loc: Sec 4.1, Proof of Prop. 2, p.10; Sec 2.1, p.7
C2.4.quote: distance-based ranking which are resolved arbitrarily in the reported rankings
C2.4.note: Metric d has separate notation from rankings and the text speaks of reported rankings; but rankings are required to be consistent with d, so IDS would also fit; DIST chosen as listed first.

C3.1.loc: Checked Sec 1 Introduction, Sec 2 Preliminaries, Secs 3-5, Sec 6 Conclusion
C3.1.note: No analysis models voters submitting rankings different from their metric preferences; strategic behaviour mentioned only for prior work.

C3.2.quote: each voter ranks candidates from closest to furthest
C3.2.note: Stated in words that rankings follow distances; formalized as consistency of the metric with the rankings (Sec 2.1).

C3.3.quote: each voter ranks candidates from closest to furthest
C3.3.note: No reason given why voters rank according to distances; footnote 2 justifies ordinal elicitation, not sincerity.

C4.1.note: Costs are metric distances; a metric is consistent with a ranking if d(v,a) <= d(v,b) whenever a is ranked above b.

C5.1.loc: Lemma 2, Sec 2.2, p.8; Theorem 5, Sec 5.2, p.17
C5.1.quote: the distortion of every plurality dominant candidate is at most 3
C5.1.note: Distortion (social cost) in results; Pareto property also discussed in Sec 5.3.

C5.2.quote: The (utilitarian) social cost of a candidate 𝑐 under a metric 𝑑
C5.2.note: Distortion is evaluated on metric distances; the Pareto property discussion (Sec 5.3) is on rankings, but distortion is the main welfare criterion.

VOT.note: Voters submit rankings consistent with distances and veto per fixed algorithmic procedure.
